description:
Found 2026-07-27 by the ub-lp9.21 Spec/Plan probe, which was verifying a DIFFERENT claim and turned this up as a by-product. Miguel scoped it OUT of the ub-lp9.21 fix and into its own issue, in the same v1.0.1 patch slot, so it gets a proper diagnosis instead of widening a PR that is already large.

OBSERVATION: a JSON-RPC frame carrying a DUPLICATE `id` member in the envelope is not decoded as the request it reads as. The duplicate collapses and the frame degrades to a shape the server treats as a NOTIFICATION, so NO response is emitted at all and a client waiting on that id hangs indefinitely. This is a distinct defect from ub-lp9.21's discriminant flip: there the wrong action executes, here nothing answers.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY FOLDED INTO ub-lp9.21: it cannot be reported through the in-band structured-error channel, because there is no usable request id to answer on — any rejection is necessarily an out-of-band protocol fault. Miguel's binding decision for ub-lp9.21 was in-band rejection, so covering this there would have contradicted it.

ALSO CORRECTED HERE, because the record was wrong: the earlier ub-lp9.21 analysis stated that the JSON-RPC envelope is immune to duplicate keys BECAUSE its typed struct fields receive serde's duplicate-field detection. The probe established that this mechanism claim is WRONG. Envelope duplicates are not rejected by duplicate-field detection; they degrade to an unknown-request shape answered with a method-not-found protocol error — and, in the `id` case, to no answer at all. The observable outcome for `method`/`name` is still a rejection, so the ub-lp9.21 blast-radius conclusion is unaffected, but the reason differs and this issue is the part that is genuinely open.

INVESTIGATE FIRST, then decide the fix. Do not assume the duplicate is the only path to the notification reinterpretation — establish what the decoder actually does, and whether other envelope members degrade the same way.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- The behaviour is reproduced live over raw JSON-RPC stdio bytes and documented: what is sent, what the server decodes it as, and what (if anything) the client receives.
- Established whether members other than `id` produce the same silent-notification degradation.
- A decision is recorded on the response: reject the frame as a protocol fault, or accept the degradation as conforming behaviour with an explicit rationale. If rejected, the channel is necessarily out-of-band and the spine's in-band argument-boundary promise must be reconciled to say so.
- Regression coverage at the raw-bytes wire level; note that the existing test harness serializes a value object and is structurally incapable of expressing a duplicate member, so the ub-lp9.21 raw-bytes capability is a prerequisite.
- No frame can leave a conforming client waiting with no response and no diagnostic.
title: Bug: a duplicate envelope `id` reinterprets a request as a notification — the client gets no response and hangs

description: Pre-existing, intermittent CI flake, unrelated to any current feature work — surfaced (not caused) by PR #429's CI run. In crates/unblock-model/tests/proptest_model_roundtrip.rs the strategies arb_issue_type() and arb_status() include a Custom arm generated from "[a-zA-Z]{1,12}", which can (rarely) produce a string equal to a CANONICAL variant name (issue_type: Task/Bug/Epic; status: Open/InProgress/Blocked/Closed). serde serializes Custom("Bug") to the wire string "Bug" and deserializes "Bug" back to the canonical IssueType::Bug, so the round-trip is NOT identity for those colliding strings and the prop_assert_eq!(left, right) fails. Observed on PR #429: issue_type_roundtrip failed with left=Custom("Bug") right=Bug after 97 successes (proptest saved regression cc 86c50f4d...). status_roundtrip carries the same latent defect (passed by luck this run). The model normalization (Custom("Bug") == Bug on the wire) is arguably correct; the DEFECT is in the test generator, which must exclude the canonical variant names from the Custom arm (e.g. prop_filter rejecting the known names, or a charset/shape disjoint from them). Fix lives entirely in the unblock-model test file; a plain `gh run rerun --failed` unblocks any PR that trips it meanwhile (rare seed). Acceptance: the Custom arms cannot generate a canonical variant name; the roundtrip proptests are deterministic-green across repeated runs (bump proptest cases locally to confirm).
title: proptest roundtrip generators emit Custom(canonical-name) → intermittent CI flake in unblock-model

Note this puts the SPINE (high tier) on this issue's side; `invalid_params` is pinned only at docs/plans/crates/unblock-mcp.md:26, the lowest tier, and descriptively. ### MIGUEL'S DECISION (2026-07-21) **v1.0.1 fixes BOTH arms** — not arm (a) alone. Accepted consequence: rejecting unknown fields emits `additionalProperties:false` into all 8 advertised inputSchemas, moving CONTRACT_HASH and forcing CONTRACT_VERSION v1.5 -> v1.6 inside a patch release, and turning previously-accepted calls into rejections. ## Spec/Plan complete + Miguel's rulings (2026-07-21) — workflow wf_eed82e64-80c

Plan file: scratchpad/v101-mcp-boundary-plan.md (9 sections). Design Review gate running as wf_900a4bbb-44f.

### MIGUEL RULED (both blocking forks closed)
1. **The input tightening ships in v1.0.1 as a DEFECT FIX, not a 2.0.0 break.** Decisive evidence: docs/PRD.md:175 — the FR-20 `[must]` acceptance criterion — already promises "tool input is schema-validated (`schemars`) and rejects oversized/invalid args". Today's code therefore FAILS a shipped must-AC; fixing it is not a behaviour change to any working call, since the only inputs newly rejected are ones currently destroyed in silence.
2. **Contract-surface scope for v1.0.1 = the CONTRACT_HASH gate widening (B2) ONLY.** outputSchema and serde aliases defer to v1.1 as two new issues.

### Feasibility SETTLED — the expensive branch is dead
`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` DOES work with `#[serde(flatten)]` on the workspace serde 1.0.228. Independently re-verified by the orchestrator against a pinned scratch crate replicating the real flatten shape:
```
GOOD -> Ok("ok")
TYPO -> Err(Error("unknown field `descriptionn`", line: 1, column: 32))
```
serde_derive emits a post-flatten leftover scan; the documented "incompatible with flatten" restriction is stale. Cost collapses from 22 hand-written deserializers to ~10 one-line attributes on OUTER containers.

**Three placement rules are load-bearing:**
- `deny` on a flatten TARGET is a silent no-op — outer containers only.
- `deny` is NOT recursive — each nested non-flattened struct needs its own (DepInput confirmed).
- `deny` ALONE converts facet (b) into facet (a): all rejections would arrive as out-of-band -32602. **(a) and (b) MUST co-land.** Never split them.

### Recommended design (plan §3, pending the Review gate)
New `crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/args.rs`: a crate-local `Parameters<T>` — deliberately shadowing rmcp's by name — whose `FromContextPart` stores raw `context.arguments` WITHOUT deserializing, making rmcp's -32602 arm (tool.rs:185-195) structurally unreachable, and whose `JsonSchema` delegates to T (hash-neutral on its own).

Ordered prologue on the RAW value, in one shared method:
1. `enforce_quota` on the raw payload — closes (c); DELETE `preflight` (server.rs:101-109 measures the re-serialized TYPED value — that IS the bug).
2. Strip `_`-prefixed reserved keys AFTER measurement, so `_meta` is neither a bypass channel nor falsely rejected.
3. `from_value::<T>` under serde_path_to_error with deny_unknown_fields — closes (b).
4. Map failures to `StructuredError{VALIDATION_FAILED, hint, context{field,kind}}` via the existing `err_json` — closes (a).

**FLAGGED TO THE REVIEW GATE, not accepted:** the name-shadowing is load-bearing (rmcp-macros `find_parameters_type_in_sig` matches the last path-segment ident `Parameters`; any other name silently degrades all 8 inputSchemas to empty). A maintainer "fixing" the import back to rmcp's silently reinstates the bug. Documented fallback is `#[tool(input_schema=...)]`. The gate rules on this, not the orchestrator.

### Scope changes to this issue
- **ub-lp9.19 (quota) FOLDS INTO THIS PR** — (c)'s fix IS the prologue ordering in the new seam and cannot be implemented independently. Issue stays open for tracking; closes on the same merge.
- **B2 gate widening folds in too**, no new issue: CONTRACT_HASH widened to the ordered triple (capabilities(), schema_bundle(), aggregate_tool_router().list_all()), plus an assertion that `list_all()[i].input_schema == schema_for_type::<T>()` so the extractor can never silently go dark, plus a transport-level channel matrix (a hash cannot express a channel).
- Contract consequence: schemars emits `additionalProperties:false` per oneOf arm -> schema_bundle() bytes move -> **CONTRACT_VERSION v1.5 -> v1.6 + CONTRACT_HASH re-pin**. Additive within 1.x per D35.
- ONE PR for cascade + (a)+(b)+(c) + B2: they share the single v1.6 bump and one golden re-bless. Splitting burns v1.7 and splits the re-bless in two — precisely when a bad golden slips through.

### HYPOTHESIS FALSIFIED — do not carry it forward
The theory that a degraded `tools/list` schema was the proximate cause is **wrong**. Over real JSON-RPC, `tools/list[i].inputSchema` is byte-identical to `schema_bundle()[tool].input` for all 8 tools — full oneOf, 66 required entries, `comment.add` correctly declaring `required:["action","issue_id","body"]`. The "Input constraint: Provide parameters for exactly one of..." prose has ZERO hits in the repo and ZERO in rmcp-1.7.0/src: the MCP *client's* renderer synthesizes it. No doc or commit message may assert that causal chain. Per M6, nothing asserts "returns OK" as server behaviour either.

### Tests (plan §5)
New `crates/unblock-cli/tests/error_channel.rs` (must live in cli — mcp_round_trip.rs precedent), needing a new `McpClient::call_tool_envelope` because today's `call_tool` asserts the error member away and structurally cannot express this class. Matrix: 8 tools x 3 malformations asserting `resp.error is None` (the channel invariant no hash can express), isError true, VALIDATION_FAILED, retryable false, non-empty hint, context.field. Plus the (c) unknown-key regression WITH its known-key control as a pair, nested-deny coverage, `_meta` acceptance, and happy-path non-vacuity via a flattened `agent_name`.

**Highest-risk failure mode:** a missed nested `deny` attribute leaves facet (b) live SILENTLY with a green suite. The per-container mutation expectations are the only guard.

## CORRECTION to comment #8, + Review gate verdict + Miguel's 3 rulings (2026-07-21)

### CORRECTION — retract "Storage is NOT implicated"
Comment #8 (and the earlier diagnosis comment) stated flatly that **storage is not implicated**. That is FALSE AS A GENERAL CLAIM and must not be carried forward. It is true only for the comment-add write path, which is what was actually probed.

Verified directly in the tree (2026-07-21): `crates/unblock-storage/src/libsql/deps.rs:86-96` binds **5 of 6** columns —
```
INSERT INTO dependencies (issue_id, depends_on_id, type, created_at, created_by)
```
`DepInput.metadata` is **accepted, typed, and published in the schema, then silently discarded at L2**. That is facet (b)'s exact harm — a silent drop behind `isError:false` — one layer BELOW where the L7 seam can reach. Reachable both via the `dep` tool and via `CreateInput.deps`.

Second survivor, same class: `crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/bulk_markdown.rs:202` — `Section::Unknown => {} // ignore unknown sections.` — with a test asserting the drop as correct behaviour. Consequence if unaddressed: after the fix the SAME tool would reject `descriptionn` on `create` and swallow `### Descriptoin` on `create_bulk`, and the rewritten FR-20 AC would be false the day it was written.

### Design Review gate: PASS_WITH_MUST_FIXES (wf_900a4bbb-44f, 4 adversarial lenses + coordinator)
All four lenses returned pass_with_must_fixes. The design CORE survived independent re-verification on every axis and is **adopted, not revisitable**: the deferring `Parameters<T>` seam (the rmcp macro really does match on the last path-segment ident — verified in both 1.7 and 1.8), `deny_unknown_fields` coexisting with flatten and internally-tagged enums, the three placement rules, the byte-identical JsonSchema delegation, and the v1.5->v1.6 bump.

What the gate rejected was the plan's periphery. 11 must-fixes, 16 should-fixes, full text appended as "## REVIEW GATE (2026-07-21)" in the plan file. The four that change the shape:
- **MF#2 — DELETE the `_`-prefix strip.** Premise was false: `_meta`/`task` are SIBLINGS of `arguments` on `CallToolRequestParams` (rmcp model.rs:2956-2967) and are destructured away at tool.rs:44-49, so a conformant `_meta` never reaches `context.arguments`. The blanket strip protected nothing while making `{"action":"show","id":"x","_junk":"LOST"}` silently accepted — reopening facet (b) on a new path, permanently.
- **MF#3 — the proposed FR-12 AC was demonstrably FALSE.** `params.arguments=42` fails during `CallToolRequestParams` deserialization BEFORE `ToolCallContext::new`, so no args.rs seam reaches it; unknown tool names likewise stay out-of-band by design. Must be scoped, not absolute.
- **MF#5 — §3.5/§5.4 were UNCOMPILABLE.** `server.rs:82` declares `fn aggregate_tool_router()` — private (verified) — and the input types are `pub(crate)` while `contract_suite.rs` is an external crate. Pin against `schema_bundle()` instead (pub at schema.rs:73); stronger pin, no type exposure.
- **MF#1 — the highest-risk vacuity hole.** Replace "sweep for others" with a MECHANICAL guard: assert every object subschema in each of the 8 published inputSchemas carries `additionalProperties:false`, recursing oneOf/$defs/items. Note `CreateInput` needs its OWN attribute — the enum-level one does not reach the newtype variant `Create(Box<CreateInput>)`, so omitting it leaves the highest-traffic action silently lossy WHILE LOOKING COVERED.

The cascade also under-enumerated: 4 more Class-1 sites including a second PRD-level one (PRD:235, the NFR-18 threat model — the exact NFR facet (c) violates), plus an entire unenumerated doc class created by the folded-in B2 widening (~20 sites incl. code doc-comments), and two hard-RED `assert_eq!` pins missing from the v1.6 re-pin list.

### MIGUEL RULED (2026-07-21) — all three at the widest scope
1. **Both L2/out-of-seam facet-(b) survivors ENTER D42.** `create_bulk`'s ignored sections AND `dep.metadata`. Accepted cost: the dep.metadata fix is an **L2 storage change**, breaking the plan's "nothing below L7 touched" and widening the Verify surface during a data-integrity patch; the `bulk_markdown` test that asserts the drop must be INVERTED. Benefit: the rewritten FR-20 AC becomes true rather than true-by-omission.
2. **NFR-18 "per-request bytes" = the whole JSON-RPC `params`, and it closes NOW.** `params._meta`/`params.task` are unmeasured today — a 300000-byte blob was reproduced passing the 256 KiB cap (options.rs:79). `server.rs:144-156` already holds the whole params object, so the size check moves up. Without this the plan could not honestly claim to close a bypass channel.
3. **The B2 public-surface addition is accepted** — a `#[doc(hidden)] pub` accessor for the router descriptors, cascading to `tests/public_api.rs` and the spine §5 interface table.

### Consequence to face honestly
Scope now spans L2 + L7, inverts an existing asserted-behaviour test, and adds public surface. The roadmap:88 "maintenance only" rewrite must say this plainly rather than paper over it — that line is no longer merely strained, it is false as written.

NEXT: plan revision folding the 11 must-fixes + 16 should-fixes + these 3 rulings, then Implement. Implementation must NOT start from the current plan text.

## Done-gate resolved: runtime assertions carry the weight, the script is demoted to lexical (2026-07-21, wf_3fb5d1f2-8b5 + wf_90f67b29-1b9)

### The executable done-gate was built, broken, hardened, and broken again
R7 replaced the prose counts with an executable script. A falsification pass then PROVED it passes vacuously — exit 0, "DONE-GATE PASSED (6 checks)", on a tree with zero behavioural change. Five bypass vectors were fixed, each with a watched fail-then-pass reproduction. A second adversarial pass broke it again with two NEW vectors that are the important ones:

**V2c — attribute FORM is not attribute SEMANTICS.**
```rust
#[serde(expecting = "an object" /* deny_unknown_fields */)]
```
rustc's lexer discards the block comment inside the attribute; the gate's regex does not. Thirteen containers spelled that way and CHECK 3 prints *"all 13 non-exempt input containers deny unknown fields"* — while a test executed on the same tree deserializes `{"kind":"ready","TOTALLY_UNKNOWN_ARG":42}` successfully.

**V2d — closing the DOCUMENT without closing the RUNTIME.** A 25-line `closed()` post-processor stamping `additionalProperties: false` onto every object node of each published inputSchema turns all 45 subschema violations green, keeps all 17 contract_suite tests passing, and changes nothing about what serde accepts. The cargo freshness proof — which resisted every laundering attempt and is genuinely sound — only proves snapshot == live DOCUMENT, and the document is produced by `schema_bundle()`, which the implementer writes. In review this is indistinguishable from the real fix; the repo already uses `#[schemars(extend("type" = "object"))]` for exactly that class of document-level stamp.

### The structural conclusion
**SIX of six checks assert over implementer-authored text** — not four, as the rescoped header claimed. Five patches to five spellings did not change the category: every new bypass was a different move against the same weakness. A doc-cascade gate is weak BY CATEGORY because the thing being checked and the thing doing the checking come from the same hand.

The falsification pass supplied the exit, and it was in the plan all along:
> a source-text check cannot decide this. Ask the compiler — a per-container assertion that `serde_json::from_str::<T>` REJECTS an unknown key. That is the §5.8 mutation table, and it is the only honest form of check 3.

A test that deserializes cannot be satisfied by annotation. No spelling, comment, or post-processor defeats it, because it does not read what was written — it executes what was compiled.

### MIGUEL RULED (2026-07-21) — R8
**The behavioural done-condition is runtime assertions; the script is demoted to lexical doc-cascade only.**
- Per input container: an assertion that `from_str::<T>` REJECTS a payload with an unknown key, and ACCEPTS the equivalent well-formed payload (the accept half is the non-vacuity guard). Already specified in §5.8 — it now carries the weight rather than supplementing a text check.
- The script keeps only the genuinely lexical checks over the doc cascade and the mechanical contract re-pin, with the four still-overstated SCOPE sentences corrected to lexical claims: it asserts that no live line matching a case-sensitive `schemars` token and one of five framing words survives — a result about five spellings, not about the document being true.
- No third hardening round. V2d is indistinguishable from legitimate work in review, so no static check can catch it; a sixth patch would be a sixth spelling.

### Proportion, recorded honestly
The behavioural change is ~10 serde attributes, one seam file, one missing storage bind, three markdown rejections, and their tests. The verification apparatus around it consumed more workflow rounds than the change will consume lines. That was defensible for a data-integrity patch on a GA product — and the apparatus did earn its keep: it falsified four confident orchestrator claims, caught a false `[must]` AC twice, an uncompilable pin, a strip built on a false premise, and a gate that greened an untouched tree. But the part worth keeping was specified by r3, and everything after it was the apparatus auditing itself.

NEXT: Implement, as an isolated-worktree team per PROCESS §4.

Understand phase complete (diagnosis only; no code changed). Eleven-agent workflow: five live-repro agents on separate throwaway workspaces, two source/contract tracers, two independent design passes, one adversarial verifier, one coordinator. Full report: scratchpad DIAGNOSIS-ub-lp9.20.md (also summarised here so this thread stands alone).

REPRODUCED LIVE over the real JSON-RPC stdio wire on binary 1.0.1-rc.2, from a clean init. The reviser's original reading was right in substance but incomplete: there are three distinct outcomes, and the loud one is the least dangerous.

1. Loud partial commit. A create whose dep names a non-existent dependent issue returns a database error naming a foreign-key constraint failure, yet the issue row is already committed with no edges, and it is immediately offered by the ready query. The error is marked retryable, so a client that obeys that flag mints a fresh orphan on every retry.

2. Silent third-party corruption (worst, and previously unrecorded anywhere). A create whose dep names an existing but unrelated issue returns success with no error at all. The new issue gets zero edges and reports ready; the edge lands on the unrelated issue, which silently drops out of the ready set. That issue's updated_at does not move, so nothing signals the mutation. Verified directly by the orchestrator, not only by an agent.

3. Silent dangling blocker. A create whose dep names a non-existent blocker also returns success and plants a permanently unresolvable blocker, because the dependencies table has a foreign key on the dependent column only, not on the blocker column. This class is wider than this issue: it is a schema property and is reachable from the dependency-add tool and from sync import as well, not only from create.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is smaller than this issue's own premise assumed. The storage layer already does the right thing: the shared per-record insert body inserts the issue's own dependency list inside the same immediate transaction and anchors every edge to the issue's own id, ignoring the client-supplied dependent id. The engine's single-create path simply never populates that list (the built issue falls through to its default, leaving dependencies empty) and instead loops separate dependency-add calls afterwards, each its own transaction. So no storage trait change is required, contrary to the observation recorded when this issue was filed. The bulk create path and sync import are both already correct for the partial-commit and misattachment classes.

WHY IT MATTERS, with evidence. A second, genuinely separate server process was handed the wrongly-ready issue by the ready query and claimed it cleanly while its intended blocker was still open, with no race involved. Nothing detects any of it: doctor reports integrity ok, the foreign-key and integrity pragmas pass, the cycle report is clean, and the ready and blocked views agree with each other, so there is no cross-view disagreement to notice. The corrupted state exports into the committed JSONL record and re-imports into a teammate's workspace through an ordinary git pull.

ONE COMPANION FINDING THAT ANY FIX MUST CARRY. The seeded insert path does not run the gating-cycle check and silently skips a repeated edge, whereas the dependency-add path rejects both. Routing create deps through the seeded path as it stands would therefore silently remove a guard that fires in production today. Verified: the cycle check has exactly two call sites, the dependency-add path and the reparent path, and neither is the seeded insert.

CORRECTIONS the adversarial pass forced, all adopted. Three tests do put a dependency array on a create payload but all are argument-boundary tests rejected before the engine, so the accurate statement is that no test reaches the engine create with a non-empty dependency array. The bulk path does not carry a latent misattachment: it re-anchors such an edge rather than misplacing it. The design spine's load-bearing falsehood is the verb describing how the edges are resolved, not the already-hedged transaction wording. One suspected sync-import defect was killed as a false lead: its zero dependency count is documented and intentional.

NEXT: the forks go to Miguel. Severity and release slot are reserved for him by this issue's own acceptance criteria; also open are the meaning of the client-supplied dependent id on the create arm, whether the dangling-blocker class belongs here or in its own issue, and where the restored cycle guard lives given that the shared body is also used by bulk create and import.

comments.text:
Decide phase complete. Miguel ruled on all four forks; the diagnosis above is the evidence base.

1. MEANING OF THE CLIENT-SUPPLIED DEPENDENT ID ON THE CREATE ARM: strict implicit ownership. The field becomes optional; when absent the edge binds the id the server just minted, inside the same transaction as the issue row. A present foreign id is REJECTED with a validation error rather than silently corrupting a third party. Contract version moves from 1.6 to 1.7; the schema change is additive, since relaxing a required entry is pure widening and the field stays on the wire. One behavioural break is ratified deliberately: a payload that today corrupts in silence will now error.

Miguel's own reasoning, which is sharper than the design reports and is the ruling's rationale: a dependency cannot exist without its endpoints, so the edge belongs to the issue being created, so the field can only ever hold one correct value. A field whose only correct value the client cannot derive is not a field, it is a trap. That framing is what rejects the two alternatives that keep a cross-issue meaning: a sentinel that preserves foreign ids exists precisely to let a create mutate a SECOND issue's graph, and letting the client mint the id hands over a responsibility the engine owns.

The decisive evidence that the mechanism is already present and correct: bulk create was run live with two issues where the second declares a dependency on the first by a symbolic intra-document handle. One call, one transaction, correct result, and the client never knew either minted id. Single create is the outlier, not the missing capability.

Accepted cost, stated openly: after this change a single call can express only "the new issue is blocked by an existing one", not the inverse. Creating an issue that blocks an existing one becomes a create followed by a dependency add. Under the ruling's own premise that is the correct outcome, not a regression: creating one issue should not silently rewrite another issue's graph.

2. SCOPE OF THE DANGLING-BLOCKER CLASS: its own issue, resolved next. This issue closes the partial commit and the misattachment, both exclusive to the create path. The dangling-blocker class is a schema property reachable from three entry points and carries a genuine sub-fork of its own about whether the guard applies to import, since applying it would make a previously exported record un-importable.

3. WHERE THE RESTORED CYCLE GUARD LIVES: on a create-specific path, not in the shared per-record insert body. Rationale: that body is also used by bulk create and by import, bulk create today commits a genuine mutual cycle atomically, and moving the guard into the shared body could make an already-exported record un-importable. Changing bulk and import semantics is explicitly out of scope here.

4. SEVERITY AND RELEASE SLOT: patch release 1.0.1. Reachable in one ordinary call with no race and no unusual configuration, undetectable by every existing diagnostic, and the recommended fix is additive and small at the engine layer. The roadmap patch section must gain the entry and its passing mention elsewhere must become a pointer.

NEXT: Spec/Plan phase, then the design review gate.

It carries the new decision row in the product document with reciprocal cross-references on the two rows it interacts with (the bulk-create decision, whose clause deliberately left the single-create path unchanged, and the dependency-edge-persistence decision, which explicitly carved this defect out); strengthened acceptance criteria on the create-surface and dependency-graph requirements; a retired carve-out and a new entry in the silent-drops register; twelve edits to the interface specification including about thirty lines of new normative contract; three crate plans; both roadmaps including the hand-maintained rendered one; the decision-range strings bumped at their three sites; and a new executable done-gate script wired into the required continuous-integration doc-lint job.

TWO CHECKS THE ORCHESTRATOR RAN PERSONALLY. The existing doc-lint passes on the cascade: nineteen documents, six classes clean. The new done-gate script is provably non-vacuous: run against the main branch it reports fifty documentation-side hits, and against the cascade it reports zero, so it kills exactly the framing the cascade retired. Its only remaining residue is in the crates directory, which is the implementation half of this same task.

MIGUEL RULINGS TAKEN THIS PHASE. First, the rejection of a client-supplied edge owner is SYNTACTIC: any present value is rejected at the boundary, and the new engine-owned input type carries no owner field at all, so a misattached edge becomes unrepresentable below layer seven rather than merely validated. He confirmed this after being shown live that the one payload it withdraws - a create under a parent whose declared edge owner correctly predicts the child id about to be minted - works only when the guess is exactly right, and that with a stale guess the same payload returns a duplicate-dependency error while still committing an orphaned issue into the ready set. Under implicit ownership that client omits the field and gets the same result, so no capability is lost. Second, the dangling-blocker class in ub-lp9.25 ships in the SAME patch cut, because this decision strictly increases exposure to it: the foreign-key failure that today masks a bogus blocker id disappears.

THE GATE VERDICT: FAIL. Four adversarial lenses ran; three returned pass-with-corrections and one returned fail, and the coordinator went with the one that had actually tested its claims, re-opening every file itself rather than counting votes. Thirteen defects survived that re-reading. None of them touches the design shape, which the gate found sound, and none reopens a ruling. They fall into four groups.

Four sentences the cascade added to authoritative documents are false about code a reader can check. The most serious is in the decision row itself: it says the shipped storage implementation does not move, while the same row places the new guards inside that implementation's own create body. The correct distinction is between the trait signature and every implementor's method set, which genuinely do not move, and the shipped body, which does. Four lower-authority documents repeat the unscoped version, so the product document currently reads stricter than the interface contract, inverting the document hierarchy.

One thing is genuinely not implementable as written. The interface contract makes the wire edge-owner field optional and asserts nothing else references that type - but three places in Rust do, including the dependency-add path, which builds the same struct and hands its owner straight into a model type whose field is non-optional. The specification must name the resolution rather than leave an implementer to reach for a default that would write an empty-string edge owner. Separately, the duplicate-edge guard is specified to run after everything is staged in the transaction using a key that is itself a transaction query, which means it either fires on every create or can never fire.

The done-gate cannot see part of what it advertises: its pattern for one retired phrasing matches nothing because the live text carries an extra word, its rule for the superseded clause pins one of three spellings, and it has no predicate over either file the fix actually lands in - so it could go green on a tree where the engine and storage change never happened.

Two tracking gaps. The orchestrator had created ub-lp9.25 in the live database but never re-exported the git record, so six normative sites cited an issue the committed export did not contain; that is now fixed by a fresh export carrying thirty-seven records. And the headline wire behaviour of the whole decision - that a present edge owner is rejected and never silently ignored - had no test cell in any document, so an adapter that simply dropped the field would have passed every other cell.

TWO SMALL RULINGS THE ORCHESTRATOR TOOK, open to Miguel's objection: the new roadmap entry for ub-lp9.25 keeps its highest-priority marker, on the same grounds the two preceding decisions carry it; and the sentence recording the co-ship ruling is dated the thirtieth of July, matching the row's own habit of dating rulings.

NEXT: repair round, then the gate re-runs on the repair. Process allows one repair round before this must be escalated rather than looped again.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Implement phase complete. Two stages in isolated worktrees, both with a working compiler, so nothing below is an unverified claim; the orchestrator then re-ran the whole check set independently.

WHAT LANDED, on branch worktree-wf_0248b42f-38c-2, nine commits on top of main: seven of specification cascade, then the code, then the tests and goldens.

At the engine layer the session gained its own declared-edge input type carrying the blocker id, the dependency type and the optional metadata, and deliberately NO source field. That is the load-bearing design choice: a misattached edge is now unrepresentable below the wire boundary rather than merely rejected at it. The create path stamps the minted id onto each edge, seeds them onto the built issue, and the loop of separate dependency writes is deleted. The bulk path, which consumes the same input type, stamps the same way; its own semantics are untouched.

At the storage layer the cycle checker was split behaviour-neutrally into a transaction-scoped graph load and a pure reachability check, and the two restored guards live in the create wrapper's own transaction, around the shared per-record insert rather than inside it. The duplicate check is an in-memory scan over the declared list on the same type-insensitive key the dedicated dependency-add path uses, because the shared body skips a repeat silently and so the transaction never holds evidence of one. The cycle check loads the graph once, after staging, so every prospective edge is present before any reachability probe. The storage trait doc now states that create persists the seeded relations re-anchored on the issue's own id, which is the omission that caused this defect to be mis-sized when it was filed.

At the wire the source field became optional and any present value is rejected before the engine is reached, with a hint that explains why the field has exactly one derivable-only-by-the-server value and names the two-step workaround. The dependency-add tool stopped routing through the shared wire type and builds the model dependency directly, since its own source id is a real, required, client-known id. The contract version moved to unblock.mcp.v1.7 with the hash re-pinned and the goldens re-blessed in the same commit.

VERIFIED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, personally, on the final tree: format check clean; clippy across the workspace with all targets and all features and warnings denied, clean, with no suppression added; the full test suite at one thousand five hundred and thirty-nine passing and zero failing; the feature-gated storage contract suite, which a plain workspace run does not reach, passing; snapshots with nothing to review; the documentation lint at nineteen documents and six classes clean; the layering check clean; the knowledge lint clean; and both executable done-gates exiting zero, this decision's own gate having gone from thirty-three reported lines to none.

AND PROVED LIVE AT THE WIRE, on a fresh workspace, with a binary built from this branch, against the three cases reproduced at the start of this issue. A create whose declared edge names a non-existent dependent is now rejected and persists NOTHING, where before it committed an edgeless issue straight into the ready set. The same shape naming an unrelated existing issue is rejected and that issue's graph is untouched, where before the edge silently landed on it. And with the field omitted the create succeeds, the edge anchored on the minted id, with the edge metadata round-tripping.

TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, both stated rather than left to be found. The acceptance criterion asking for a wire-level regression test over a create whose edge names a non-existent BLOCKER is covered at the wire, but it asserts only what this decision actually guarantees for that input - one indivisible act, anchored on the minted id - because whether such a blocker should be REFUSED is the separate issue ub-lp9.25, which Miguel ruled ships in the same patch cut but as its own change. The test carries that boundary in its own doc-comment and is written to start failing when that issue lands. Second, this commit carries neither the knowledge-layer run-report nor the tracker record re-export; both are orchestrator actions and land at the tracking step, before the pull request.

NEXT: the Verify quality gate, four adversarial lenses including a mutation pass that will break the fix seven different ways to establish which properties are actually pinned by a dying test rather than merely accompanied by a passing one.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Verify quality gate: PASS WITH MUST-FIX. Four adversarial lenses - a mutation pass, a code review, a security and input-robustness lens, and a regression and document-truth lens - then a coordinator who re-checked every finding against the source rather than tallying verdicts. Full report in the session scratchpad; the substance is here.

THE MUTATION PASS IS WHY THIS GATE EARNED ITS KEEP. It broke the fix seven ways, each mutant in its own throwaway worktree, and recorded which properties a DYING test actually pins rather than which are merely accompanied by a passing one.

Nine properties are now empirically pinned. Atomicity: re-adding the old per-edge write loop killed three cells - and the state-invisible variant, where the loop swallows its own error so the final database state is identical, was caught ONLY by the call-counter cell, which is precisely why that cell was demanded. The boundary rejection of a client-supplied edge source: a silently-dropping adapter killed the wire-level cell. Its error discriminator, the duplicate guard, the cycle guard, the ordering property, edge-metadata propagation, and the storage-layer re-anchoring each died on named cells. Most importantly for regression: moving both guards into the shared per-record insert body killed five cells across four crates, including the import leg - so the silent-regression mode this design was shaped to avoid is genuinely watched.

TWO PROPERTIES WERE NOT PINNED, AND THREE TEST DOC-COMMENTS CLAIMED THEY WERE. The engine stamping the minted id onto each declared edge, and the engine stamping the session actor: three separate mutants against the first and one against the second all SURVIVE the entire fifteen-hundred-test suite. The reason is subtle and worth recording, because it will recur. The storage layer re-anchors the edge regardless - it binds the issue's own id and never reads the supplied source - and the engine returns a re-read of the persisted row. So every existing assertion observes what the storage layer wrote, never what the engine wrote. The guarantee is real; it is delivered one layer below where the normative clause declares it, which leaves that clause itself untested.

That is, letter for letter, the failure class this repository has already let through twice: a coverage claim accepted by review without a mutant ever being shown to die. It was caught here before merge only because the gate refused to accept the claim on its face. The fix extends the existing counting harness to capture the issue value handed to storage, so the engine-level clause becomes observable rather than being downgraded to prose-only coverage - one cell kills all four survivors.

A HOLE IN THE DONE-GATE ITSELF. The published contract identifier is still the previous version in two places - the root README and the owning crate plan - while the code emits the new one. Both survived a green done-gate, a green documentation lint and a green knowledge lint, because the gate pinned the contract version in only two code files, the root README sits outside the documentation-lint corpus, and no rule class in either tool fires on a stale version literal. The gate's contract-pin table is being extended to cover both, with a non-vacuity proof: it must be shown to BLOCK on the stale state before being accepted as covering it.

TWO FINDINGS THE COORDINATOR DOWNGRADED after his own reading, recorded because a gate that only ever escalates is not calibrated. The security lens framed an unknown-field hint that still advertises the now-rejected argument as violating an existing invariant; re-reading the invariant and its oracle showed it concerns fields rejected at parse time, and the argument in question genuinely parses - a real contradiction in spirit, no bypass, no unbounded echo, so it is a should-fix. And the question the implementation phase could not settle - whether a lettered ride-along item in the interface specification, naming a method that is now deleted, is a stale claim - was adjudicated as correct change-instruction prose in the same style the neighbouring decision block uses, with an explicit instruction not to touch it.

Six further should-fixes are recorded and none blocks: an always-on cell for the storage re-anchor so the default test set reaches it, an arm-aware hint, one extracted helper for a stamp written three times by hand, an errors list missing two newly reachable rejections, two missing client hints, and one doc sentence that would stay true if someone broke the guard it describes.

NEXT: the four blocking items land, then the surviving mutants are re-run to prove the coverage claim empirically rather than by comment, then tracking - the record re-export and the knowledge-layer run-report, which the required continuous-integration job blocks the pull request without.

description:
Surfaced 2026-07-21 while planning ub-lp9.12 (workflow wf_bfeed9a6-ed0). PRE-EXISTING GA defect — not introduced by the ub-lp9.12 boundary change. Miguel ruled it OUT of that PR and into its own issue, so it gets a proper diagnosis rather than being fixed in passing inside a change already spanning L2+L7.

OBSERVATION: the storage trait's `create_issue` (crates/unblock-storage/src/trait_def.rs:99) takes only `&Issue` — it has no deps parameter. So an `issue create` carrying `deps` must insert the issue and its dependency edges in SEPARATE calls, which means the issue can be committed while its deps fail. The reviser additionally reported that `create.deps` unconditionally FK-fails and partial-commits; that specific claim was NOT independently verified and must be reproduced before it is treated as fact.

WHY IT MATTERS: unblock is a data-integrity tool with atomic multi-agent claim as its wedge (FR-2). A create that half-lands leaves an issue whose declared dependency graph is silently incomplete — and `query ready` is computed FROM that graph, so a dropped `blocks` edge makes a genuinely-blocked issue report as ready. That is the same class of harm as the ub-lp9.12 silent drops, one layer down.

INTERACTION: ub-lp9.12 (Miguel ruling R1-ii) adds the missing `dep.metadata` bind at L2. Metadata cannot be proven to round-trip through `create.deps` while this atomicity defect stands, so ub-lp9.12's plan must state that bound honestly rather than claim a guarantee it cannot make.

INVESTIGATE FIRST, then decide severity and release slot. Do not assume the reviser's reading is correct — reproduce it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- The actual behaviour of `issue create` with a `deps` array is reproduced live on a throwaway workspace and documented: what commits, what fails, in what order, and what the client sees.
- Whether a partial commit is reachable (and under which inputs) is established with evidence, not inferred from the trait signature.
- If confirmed: the issue and its dependency edges commit atomically, or the create fails whole with nothing persisted.
- Regression test at the live JSON-RPC wire level covering a create whose deps reference a non-existent blocker.
- The `query ready` consequence is covered: no input can produce an issue that reports ready because an edge was silently dropped.
- Severity and release slot decided by Miguel after the diagnosis, not before.
title: Bug: `issue create` with deps is non-atomic — the issue can be created while its deps fail

close_reason: Merged to main via PR #433 (2026-07-29, merge commit de3ed93) as decision D43. A duplicate JSON key in a tool call's params is now rejected in-band, fail-closed at any depth over the whole params subtree; the defect is demonstrated closed against the original exploit. Contract-neutral (no new error code, frozen hash unmoved). Six gate rounds; the sibling envelope-id defect stays tracked as ub-cnv.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Understand phase started (2026-07-27) — this task is now the active work, taken as the top-priority ready item after the knowledge-layer epic closed.

Orchestrator orientation before delegating, so the team was briefed on facts rather than guesses: the argument seam is the crate-local deferring extractor in the MCP crate's tools/args.rs. It takes the arguments the transport already parsed — an in-memory JSON object — and only then deserializes into the typed input. So the duplicate key is collapsed last-wins BEFORE any of our code runs, which is exactly why the D42 unknown-field rejection is structurally blind to it: serde does report a duplicate field, but only when deserializing from the raw byte stream, never from an already-collapsed map. This confirms the issue's own diagnosis that the fix must sit ABOVE the transport's parse, not at the D42 seam.

Understand team spawned as a Workflow (three adversarial lenses plus a coordinator): (1) BLAST RADIUS — re-verify the defect still reproduces on current main over raw stdio bytes, then enumerate all eight tools, their discriminants and arm values, naming which arms are destructive or state-changing and which flips are actually reachable; also the non-discriminant damage a last-wins duplicate enables, such as re-selecting a target id or a harder delete mode. (2) SEAM — trace the exact path from raw bytes to the typed parse and lay out every candidate interception point with its trade-offs, judged against three hard constraints: the in-band structured-error channel must stay the only failure path (the out-of-band JSON-RPC arm must remain unreachable), the published contract is frozen at GA so a fix should be contract-neutral, and the layering is enforced. (3) SPEC — quote the exact PRD and spine claims that are FALSE while this stands, establish what the JSON and MCP specs actually say about duplicate keys, survey what serde can and cannot do here with evidence, and list every doc site needing reconciliation.

The team analyses only; no implementation. Its output feeds a Decide fork for Miguel, then spec-first, then Implement and the Verify gate with a security-review lens (this is MCP input handling).

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Understand outcome + Decide (2026-07-27).

RE-VERIFIED, twice independently. A lens reproduced it over a real MCP child on raw stdio bytes, and the orchestrator then reproduced it again with its own harness on current main: a frame whose text reads as a create, carrying a second action key set to delete, returned isError false and tombstoned the target (status tombstone, deleted_at and deleted_by set). The control cell in the same run confirms the D42 unknown-field rejection is live and correctly rejecting an unknown key — it is simply blind to this.

BLAST RADIUS is total, not partial. Every key inside the arguments object, at any depth, is substitutable on all eight tools. 178 ordered shown-arm to executed-arm flips are constructible across the seven tagged tools, and 100 of those are schema-clean, meaning the payload's other fields are also valid for the arm a reader sees, so nothing in the frame looks out of place. The one non-union tool has no discriminant but is still fully target- and actor-substitutable. Executed proofs include a read frame performing a write, a dry-run delete mode flipped to permanent row removal, a dry-run import flipped to a real write of attacker-authored data, a comment redacted by a frame that reads as a list, and a non-gating dependency frame landing a gating edge.

THE EXACT BOUNDARY, which also explains why no existing test could have caught this: the JSON-RPC envelope is IMMUNE, because its fields are typed struct fields decoded from bytes and serde does report a duplicate field there. Only the arguments object is vulnerable, because it is a map. Consequently the existing argument-boundary guard, which deserializes from a string, and the whole CLI harness, which serializes a value object, are structurally incapable of even expressing this input.

TWO STRUCTURAL IMPOSSIBILITIES (these delete whole families of proposals and are not choices): a fix at the typed-parse seam or inside tool bodies cannot work, because the second key is already gone several frames earlier; and detection inside a transport decorator of the existing kind cannot work either, because that layer receives an already-parsed message. Detection and rejection must therefore live in different layers.

MIGUEL'S DECISIONS: (1) CHANNEL = IN-BAND — a duplicate-key frame comes back as a structured validation failure like every other argument error, preserving the normative in-band promise; the cheaper out-of-band framing-reject was considered and declined. (2) SCOPE = INCLUDE the second instance of the same root cause in the bd-file importer in this same fix, rather than letting it survive by silence. (3) RELEASE = the open v1.0.1 patch slot; rejecting duplicates is a behavioural break only for a client that emits them, which no conforming client does.

NOT a fork, verified: no new error code may be minted — it would move the frozen contract hash and become a breaking change under the GA stability decision. The existing validation-failure code is reused, with the duplicate-key kind carried in the error context.

ORCHESTRATOR'S D-ID CALL, open to countermand: this rides a NEW decision id rather than an amendment to D42, because the PRD already records that this sits outside D42's seam and is not closed by it, which is a separately-motivated decision under the process rule; minting it triggers the documented range bump at its three sites.

SPEC-FIRST DRIFT, surfaced not silently fixed: the interface SSOT is currently wrong where the product truth is right — an inverted hierarchy. The spine's normative argument-boundary section asserts that malformed arguments are rejected in-band and gives a CLOSED list of the exceptions; a duplicate-key frame is in neither list, being instead accepted and executed. A second spine site repeats the false claim, and the per-crate always-in-context contract doc for the MCP crate states it unqualified — the site a future session reads first. The PRD, by contrast, already discloses the gap honestly and needs only an editorial pass once the fix lands. Spec/Plan phase starts now.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Spec/Plan outcome (2026-07-27, pipeline: an empirical probe phase, then three planners, then a coordinator that wrote the package). Package is complete and marked ready for the design gate.

THE PROBE CLOSED THE FOUR LOAD-BEARING UNKNOWNS, all four verified rather than argued. The security-critical one first: the verdict carrier is WIRE-UNFORGEABLE — the type has no serialization at all, only a distinct metadata field is insertable from the wire, and an end-to-end prototype's forgery attempt failed. Second: the framework's own extractor for that carrier answers with the out-of-band protocol error when the value is absent, which would have reopened the exact arm this repo closed — so the handler must read the carrier directly, never through that extractor. Third: no dependency-feature change is needed. Fourth: the in-process test path and the real stdio path ride two different wirings that converge on the same concrete transport, so a byte-level check DOES force widening one generic bound, with a blast radius of three call sites.

A CORRECTION TO THE RECORD, surfaced by the probe against my own earlier statement. I had reported as established that the JSON-RPC envelope is immune BECAUSE its typed fields receive serde's duplicate-field detection. That mechanism claim is WRONG. Envelope duplicates are not caught that way; they degrade to an unknown-request shape. The blast-radius conclusion is unaffected, since the observable outcome for the method and tool-name members is still a rejection — but the reason differs, and the probe turned up a genuinely new defect in the process: a duplicated envelope id makes the frame decode as a notification, so NO response is emitted and a waiting client hangs. Per Miguel that is now tracked separately as ub-cnv in the same patch slot; it cannot be folded in here because with no usable id there is no in-band channel to answer on, which would contradict the in-band decision.

THE DESIGN, in short. Detection sits in an OWNED transport that replaces rather than decorates the framework's, doing read-line then scan then parse then stamp in one place — which removes an entire failure class, since a separate byte-sniffing layer would have to re-frame the stream itself and could silently desynchronise against a reader that consumes lines without emitting them. The scanner is a deserializer VISITOR rather than a hand-rolled tokenizer, so it reuses the parser's own string decoding (escape-equivalent keys compare equal) and inherits its recursion bound; it lives in the base error crate, verified to need zero layering changes. The verdict is three-state and stamped on every decoded request; rejection happens at exactly one site, and an ABSENT verdict rejects too, so an unscanned frame cannot slip through. The error reuses the existing validation-failure code with the duplicate-key kind and the offending key and path in its context, keeping the frozen contract hash unmoved. The importer arm rejects at first failure with zero writes, folded into the existing parse-error mapping rather than into its dropped-fields report.

MIGUEL'S TWO FURTHER DECISIONS, taken before implementation because reversing them later would mean re-blessing pinned tests: (1) SCAN SCOPE = the WHOLE params subtree, not just the arguments object — the broader fail-closed reading, chosen over the package's narrower default, so a future consumer of the reserved metadata cannot silently reopen the gap. The design gate must now re-examine the false-positive surface this widening creates, since the package had pinned the narrow scope as a negative test cell. (2) The duplicate-envelope-id defect goes to its own issue, as above.

Design Review gate spawned (three adversarial lenses plus a coordinator) over the package, with a standing instruction to hunt for a bypass rather than confirm the design, to re-derive the eleven claims the package itself marks unverified, and to judge whether the verification plan is genuinely non-vacuous — the existing harness is structurally incapable of expressing this input, so a green suite proving nothing is the realistic failure mode here.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Design Review gate, round 1 (2026-07-27; three adversarial lenses — bypass hunt, architecture, verification and cascade — plus a coordinator): VERDICT = PASS WITH MUST-FIXES. Seventeen blocking items, all corrections and coverage rather than a redesign; the core mechanism survived an adversarial attempt to break it.

WHAT SURVIVED, re-verified by the coordinator itself rather than taken on a lens's word: the scanner's home in the base error crate needs zero layering changes; contract-neutrality genuinely holds, because the error context is a free-form map and the code list is built from the existing enumeration, so reusing the validation-failure code cannot move the frozen hash; the rejection site is real and correctly placed, ahead of the existing quota and inside the rate-limit permit; the two structural impossibilities that force detection down at the bytes are sound; and the importer arm is right.

THE FOUR BIGGEST DEFECTS FOUND. First, the late scope widening had not propagated: twelve sites still pinned the narrow scope, INCLUDING an executable test cell asserting the exact OPPOSITE of the shipped design and a written rationale arguing AGAINST it — an implementer following the package verbatim would have built the wrong scope and written a test blessing the defect. Second, three references point at test cells that DO NOT EXIST, and the arm the package itself calls "the whole security property" — an unscanned frame must be rejected — has ZERO coverage today, because the only in-tree driver of the relevant test path performs a handshake and never calls a tool. Third, the framing contract mis-states where the byte-order-mark is stripped relative to the fallback parse, which would have shipped a protocol violation against notifications the framework silently ignores. Fourth, several test cells are UNCONSTRUCTIBLE against the real wire shapes (two nested cases cannot exist because those fields are flattened or are plain strings) and two escape-equivalence cells were written as byte-identical pairs, so a byte-comparing scanner would pass them vacuously — the precise "green suite proving nothing" failure this gate was told to hunt.

Found 2026-07-21 by the ub-lp9.12 Verify gate (wf_4efbe011-3ae), MF-3. PRE-EXISTING in GA — NOT introduced by the D42 boundary change, and NOT fixable at the D42 seam.

REPRODUCED live on a raw JSON-RPC frame:

  {"name":"issue","arguments":{"action":"create","ids":["ub-qho"],"action":"delete"}}
  -> isError:false, {"mode":"tombstone","targets":["ub-qho"]}
  -> `issue show ub-qho` confirms deleted_at / deleted_by are set.

A payload that reads as `create` executed a `delete`. Also reproduced: {"action":"create","title":"DUP1","title":"DUP2"} creates the issue titled DUP2.

MECHANISM: serde_json collapses duplicate keys (last-wins) BEFORE `parse_args` ever receives a JsonObject, so `deny_unknown_fields` structurally cannot see them. The fix must sit ABOVE rmcp's parse — a duplicate-rejecting deserializer at the transport boundary — not at the D42 seam.

SEVERITY, stated honestly: it requires a malformed payload with duplicate keys, which a conforming client does not emit; and the delete is a tombstone, so it is recoverable via restore. But this is discriminant confusion on a data-integrity tool, and every tagged-enum tool input is potentially affected, not just issue.action. The blast radius across the other 7 tools has NOT been enumerated.

INTERACTION with ub-lp9.12: that change's newly-landed text at docs/PRD.md:176 (FR-20 AC, "unknown-field and malformed arguments are rejected in-band") and docs/PRD.md:238 (NFR-18, "strictly deserialized") OVERCLAIM while this stands. Miguel ruled (2026-07-21) that ub-lp9.12 must correct that wording to disclose this residual explicitly, in the same commit, and file the fix here. Same pattern already used for ub-lp9.20.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- The duplicate-key behaviour is enumerated across ALL 8 tools and every tagged-enum discriminant, not just issue.action — with the destructive arms named.
- A duplicate key in tool arguments is rejected with the contracted in-band structured error, or an explicit, documented decision is recorded for why it is accepted.
- Regression test at the raw JSON-RPC wire level (the existing client helpers normalise the frame, so the test must construct the duplicate-key bytes directly).
- No payload can select a tool action other than the one a left-to-right reading of the frame indicates.
- The PRD/spine wording is reconciled with whatever behaviour actually ships.

## RESOLVED (2026-07-22, wf_7ab05d96-1d2) — the shipped state was already correct; the rule is now written

### The decision
Investigated the PRD decision registry rather than deciding fresh: the repo ALREADY practises a consistent rule for this, applied in ~12 cases. The discriminator it uses is MOTIVATION, not the size of the change:
- A **consequence/refinement of the SAME decision** (intent preserved — a forward-refinement or correction, NOT a reversal) → **inline amendment/addendum on the existing row, riding that D-id; no new D-id, no D-range bump**. Precedent: D29 F5-A ("an ADDENDUM to D29, NOT a new D-id — the D1..D29 range is unchanged"); D38's inline correction of D27/AD-4; the explicit D29 F4 label "a FORWARD-REFINEMENT of D27/AF-1 ... NOT a reversal".
- A change **driven by a NEW, separately-motivated decision** that supersedes part of an earlier one → **that decision's own new D-id, with reciprocal cross-refs in BOTH rows** (new: "SUPERSEDES/CORRECTS Dnn clause X"; old: inline "SUPERSEDED/amended by Dnn"), and minting the D-id triggers the D-range bump at its 3 sites (CLAUDE.md, ci-cd §2.1(a), the doc_lint.rs comment). Precedent: D37 SUPERSEDES D22's count consequence; D25 SUPERSEDES D24; D17↔D19; D14↔D31; D27/AD-4↔D38.

### Applied to this instance
The create_bulk rejections are a CONSEQUENCE of D42's own thesis (reject malformed input in-band instead of silently dropping it), not a separately-motivated decision. So they ride D42, and D42 supersedes D22 clause 2. **The shipped state is CORRECT — no D43 is needed.** Verified: PRD:125 carries "SUPERSEDES D22 clause 2", PRD:105 carries the reciprocal "SUPERSEDED by D42". This is the same pattern as D37↔D22. The orchestrator ruling O-2 (no separate D-id) matched the precedent.

### What was actually missing — now fixed
The rule was APPLIED 12 times but WRITTEN nowhere, which is why O-2 got re-litigated at all. Commit 7e329b7 adds it to docs/PROCESS.md §3 (Decisions) as one lean bullet, cross-linked to the decision-change checklist, with the D42/D22-clause-2 case cited in-rule as the worked example so it is not re-litigated again.

### Verification (the "review" for this close)
- The written rule was checked against EVERY amendment/supersession marker in PRD §4 — zero contradictions. Critically, NO case exists where a clause change was given a bare D-id purely to log the change (which the rule forbids), so the rule matches the registry as practised, not an invented convention.
- Probe green: doc-lint "19 docs, 6 classes clean", check-layering clean. PROCESS.md is not in the doc-lint corpus; CLAUDE.md untouched (it imports PROCESS.md via @, so no duplication).

Closing on merge of branch t101-d42-mcp-argument-boundary (the commit lives there). No behaviour change, docs-only, spec-first.

Miguel ruled 2026-07-21: this needs its own task at maximum priority. It was decided in-flight by the ORCHESTRATOR (ruling O-2), not by Miguel, and it is the one of the three orchestrator rulings that gets MORE expensive to overturn with time.

THE QUESTION. The D42 change adds five create_bulk rejections. Three of them (invalid `### Priority` silently defaulting, a known H3 before the first `## `, and an unknown `### ` section) directly contradict **D22 clause 2**, which decided that unknown H3 sections are IGNORED. The unterminated-fence rejection (Miguel-ratified) is a fourth behaviour change, and the empty `### ` header (orchestrator ruling O-1, Miguel confirmed OK) a fifth.

Does reversing a shipped D22 clause warrant its own PRD decision row (a D43), or is riding the existing D42 row as an explicit supersession of D22 clause 2 sufficient?

WHY IT MATTERS: D-ids are the PRD's decision registry and the CI doc-lint checks the range. If the call is wrong, the cascade renumbering is wrong at every conventional site, and a future reader looking for "when did unknown sections stop being ignored" finds a D22 row that still says they are ignored.

WHY IT IS URGENT: when this was proposed, the fix was cheap. The cascade has now LANDED. Overturning means redoing the D-range bump across every conventional site and reopening documents already closed — and the cost keeps rising while the PR sits.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- A decision is recorded, with rationale, on whether reversing a shipped D-clause requires a new D-id in this repo — as a general rule, not just for this instance.
- If a D43 is required: it is minted, the D22 clause-2 supersession is stated in both rows, and the D-range is bumped at every conventional site (CLAUDE.md, ci-cd, doc_lint.rs comment) with the doc-lint green.

- The doc-lint passes and a grep for the old framing returns zero LIVE hits (historical records excluded, and the exclusion rule written down).

description:
Filed 2026-07-22 out of the ub-lp9.12 (D42) work. A first attempt — doc-lint class (g), commit f3ab75b — scanned the doc corpus for MCP surface-count literals (tools/resources/prompts) and compared them to a count parsed from capabilities.rs. It FAILED its Verify gate (wf_8d7b0c63-ff9) and was reverted (commit a30dabc), replaced by naming the doc sites in the existing runtime count pins (contract_suite.rs).

WHY THE PROSE-SCAN APPROACH FAILED — the category weakness, so the redesign does not repeat it:
- Its historical exemption was a WHOLE-LINE marker word ({superseded, amendment, used to, ...}): a single word papers over any stale count on that line. Live proof: docs/PRD.md:367 carries "8 tools" fully exempt because the line also says "amendment (2026-07-21)". This is the SAME defeat as the SUPERSED-excuse that broke the executable done-gate earlier in the same session — a check over author-written text whose exemption is also author-written text.
- It false-positived on ordinary English: "the pool holds 4 resources per worker", "the release wizard shows 2 prompts" all fire and would block CI. Requiring an "MCP" token to disambiguate would make it MISS the bare definitional "8 tools" lines and go vacuous. That tension (precise-context vs vacuity) is unresolvable with regex over prose.
- Its anchor parser counted `(` at bracket depth 1, a proxy that under-counts a non-tuple array element (a const or `..spread`) — so a real 9 could parse as 8 and match stale docs, green forever. And it derived 5 resources where the contract pins 4 CONCRETE (the 5th is a template) — the parser's notion of "count" already disagreed with the contract.

THE LESSON (session-wide): a check that reads text the author also writes is weak by category. The only robust guards this session found are the ones that EXECUTE — `assert_eq!(capabilities().tools.len(), 8)` cannot be silenced by an annotation. The current state relies on that pin plus a human reading its lockstep-doc reminder on failure.

A REAL DESIGN would remove the human step without scanning prose. Directions to evaluate (do NOT just rebuild the prose scanner):
- Generate the count-bearing doc fragment from capabilities() at doc-build time (a single included/transcluded snippet the docs reference, so there is ONE authoritative rendering and nothing to keep in sync by hand).
- Or a doc-test / rustdoc-include that fails compilation when the rendered count and the source diverge.
- Or accept that free-prose counts are inherently editorial and instead REDUCE the number of doc sites that hardcode a count at all (fewer places to drift), which the lockstep-reminder pin already partially addresses.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- A design is chosen and recorded that makes a doc/code surface-count divergence fail a machine gate WITHOUT scanning free prose for count literals.
- The chosen mechanism cannot be silenced by adding a marker word to a line (the class-(g) failure mode).
- It distinguishes the 4-concrete-resources vs 5-total (incl. 1 template) nuance correctly, or documents why it does not need to.
- If implemented: it goes RED on a real count change (proven by execution, both directions) and does not false-positive on the live corpus or on ordinary English.
- Non-goal explicitly recorded: this is NOT a revival of prose-scanning class (g); reference commit f3ab75b and this issue's failure analysis.
title: Design a machine-enforced doc surface-count guard that does not scan free prose

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text: Description corrected after ub-lp9.20 merged. The original text said the defect is a missing foreign key on the blocker column; the roadmap's 1.0.1 slot states that the absence is DELIBERATE, because an external:* target is a legitimate blocker that no foreign key could satisfy.
