Also recorded: this mints no decision id, and the import sub-fork is still open and belongs to Miguel.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Live repro over the MCP wire on a clean throwaway workspace, driving the server binary built from this branch (server reports 1.0.1-rc.2). FOUR edge-writing entry points accept a blocker id that does not exist, not three. One: issue create with a seeded dep returns isError false and persists the edge onto the issue it just created, so a brand-new issue is born permanently blocked. Two: dep add returns added true. Three: sync import of a D5 JSONL record persists the edge. Four: sync import_bd persists it too. The roadmap slot names three entry points, so the bd one-shot import is a fourth that must either be in scope or be explicitly ruled out with a reason.

The external carve-out is live and must be preserved: dep add with the target external:JIRA-1 is accepted and stored.

Consequences observed on that workspace: all victims sit in query blocked, query ready is empty, and the dangling target is invisible to every existing diagnostic. diagnostics lint reports only missing acceptance-criteria sections, diagnostics orphans is empty, and the CLI doctor command reports health healthy and integrity ok on a workspace holding four unresolvable blockers. That is precisely the gap the doctor view in the acceptance criteria has to close.

One side observation to confirm during implementation: the D5 JSONL import reported a dependency count of zero in its import summary while the dependency edge did land, whereas the bd import reported one for the same shape. Either that counter is wrong on the D5 path or the edge is written outside the counted step.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Understand phase outcome (three review lenses plus a coordinator, then four claims re-verified by running the server, not by reading it).

SHAPE OF THE TREE. There are three production SQL bodies that insert a dependency row, reached from five wire entry points: issue create with seeded deps, dep add, sync import (both the D5 JSONL import and the bd one-shot import, which share one tail), issue update with a parent (a reparent), and issue create_bulk. The roadmap slot names three. The reparent and the bulk path are unnamed anywhere.

THE NEVER-READY SYMPTOM IS NARROWER THAN FILED. It fires only for the three direct gating types blocks, conditional-blocks and waits-for. A dangling parent-child edge does NOT make the child unready: verified by running it, the child with a phantom parent stays in the ready set. Two of the three lenses claimed otherwise and were wrong; the dissenting lens was right. The reparent path is still a real dangling-edge producer and a subject for the doctor view, but it must not be sold as a never-ready defect.

THE FACT THAT DECIDES THE IMPORT QUESTION. The exporter drops ephemeral and wisp ROWS but not the EDGES pointing at them. Verified by running an export: a durable issue blocked by an ephemeral one produced a file where the ephemeral row is absent and the edge to it is still serialized on the durable issue's line. So unblock's own export can legitimately contain an edge whose blocker is absent from the file. Guarding the import path therefore means refusing files this tool itself produces. Two further sources of the same shape: every external target is absent from any export by construction, and the D23 import-collision default of skip means a file is applied against a database where some referenced ids exist and some do not.

THE EXTERNAL PREFIX IS UNPINNED AND THE TWO LIVE IMPLEMENTATIONS DISAGREE. The ready query uses a SQL LIKE, which is case-insensitive, while the bulk parser uses a Rust starts_with, which is not. Verified live: an uppercase EXTERNAL target is treated as an external blocker by the ready query, so the issue stays ready, and is rejected as an unresolvable id by create_bulk. Worse for the carve-out: create_bulk rejects a correctly-spelled lowercase external target today, and that rejection is normatively pinned in the spine. Adding the carve-out on that path relaxes a shipped, pinned rejection.

CONSTRAINTS THAT ARE NOT NEGOTIABLE. A schema change is unauthorised by the D44 row. In-transaction means the check body must sit in the storage crate, because the transaction type never leaves it. No new error code may be minted: post-general-availability the spine calls that a breaking contract change, so the sanctioned shape is a new internal storage error variant mapped onto an existing code. A new MCP tool is forbidden, the eight-tool budget is full. Emitting the doctor view as generic findings under an existing diagnostic kind moves zero contract bytes; adding a field to the import report would force a contract bump.

TRAP FOUND IN THE D44 TEST SUITE. The wire cell written to anticipate this repair branches on whether the call errored and passes in both worlds, so when the refusal lands the cell will silently stop pinning anything while its docstring keeps claiming the input is not refused. It must be rewritten to assert the refusal specifically, or the new behaviour ships unpinned by the very test written for it.

Four forks now go to Miguel: whether import is guarded, whether the reparent and bulk paths are in scope, the external prefix and case rule, and the doctor surface.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Decide phase. Miguel ruled on four forks on 2026-07-31. His rulings, and what each one obliges.

ONE, THE IMPORT QUESTION, WHICH THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA REQUIRED BE PUT TO HIM. Ruling: guard every path, AND repair the exporter. The existence check goes into the shared per-record insert body, so the create path, both import paths and the bulk path are covered by one change; and the exporter stops emitting an edge whose target row it deliberately dropped, so an export and a re-import of it stays a working round-trip. The evidence that forced the pairing: running an export on a workspace where a durable issue is blocked by an ephemeral one produced a file with the ephemeral row absent and the edge to it still on the durable issue's line. Guarding the import without repairing the exporter would have made unblock refuse files it produces itself. Two consequences that must be honoured. The guard must be batch-aware, meaning the target must exist in the database OR anywhere in the same batch, because the shipped behaviour is that a forward reference inside one import file resolves only when the sibling was minted earlier; a naive per-record check would reject legal files. And moving the guard into the shared body deliberately reverses a clause D44 published, so this task now MINTS A NEW DECISION ID, contrary to its original charter of having none. That new row supersedes the D44 clause with reciprocal pointers in both rows, and triggers the decision-range bump at its three string sites.

TWO, SCOPE. Ruling: close all five edge-writing entry points, not the three the roadmap names. The two unnamed ones are the reparent path, which accepts a phantom parent today, and the bulk create path. Two honesty obligations ride along: the roadmap sentence that says three entry points is corrected in the same commit, and the bulk path's rejection of a correctly-spelled external target is relaxed, which is a behaviour change on a shipped, spine-pinned path and is stated plainly rather than footnoted.

THREE, THE EXTERNAL PREFIX. Ruling: case-insensitive. The principle that decided it is that the write guard must never be stricter than the read side. The ready query already treats an uppercase external target as an external blocker, so a case-sensitive guard would reject a target the reader considers legitimate. This changes no existing workspace's behaviour; it aligns the bulk parser to the query. The prefix and its case rule are pinned in the spine before any code is written, and the shared predicate lives in the model crate, which is the only layer both storage and engine may depend on.

FOUR, THE VIEW THAT LISTS THE DANGLING BLOCKERS. Ruling: a new action on the existing diagnostics tool, so an agent can ask for exactly this and nothing else, plus the same findings folded into the command-line doctor report, which is what the roadmap's wording asks for. Rejected alternatives were folding it into the existing lint findings, which costs nothing but cannot be asked for on its own, and minting a ninth tool, which would lift a self-imposed ceiling for no need. Established while answering him: the eight-tool ceiling is our own risk-mitigation rule in the spine, not the semver freeze, and the data was already fully visible over MCP; what was missing was the diagnosis, since the dependency graph loader does not join, so the phantom edge survives into the tree with nothing marking it phantom.

CONTRACT CONSEQUENCE. The new diagnostics action and its report kind move schema bytes, so this carries a further additive contract bump on top of the D44 one, with the pinned hash re-cut. It is cheap because the previous bump has not been released either; both ship in the same maintenance cut.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Spec phase, part one: the drafting pass wrote paste-ready normative text but its landing agents all died on a session limit, so nothing reached the repository. The working tree was verified clean and the promised patch file does not exist. The drafts survived on disk and are good: the cascade inventory is machine-derived rather than prose, and it caught two traps worth recording here.

FIRST TRAP. The done-gate script for the previous decision pins the contract id as a literal and demands its presence in four files, one of which must contain no other version literal at all. So the moment the readme and the crate plan move to the new contract id, that gate turns red for a reason having nothing to do with the decision it guards. The knob must move in the same commit as those files.

SECOND TRAP, and the sequencing correction it forced. The contract-id publishing sites are asserted against the code constant and against golden snapshots. Moving them in the spec commit would break the build for a change that has no code yet. So the spec commit lands normative text only and names the new contract id in NEW prose; every existing literal, and the gate knob, move later with the code.

THE EIGHT ITEMS THE DRAFTING PASS LEFT OPEN ARE NOW CLOSED by the orchestrator. They are consequences of Miguel's four rulings rather than new forks, and each is stated so he can veto it.
One: the new diagnostics action is named dangling, matching the seven existing plain-noun kinds.
Two: the contract becomes version one point eight, following the two bumps already in this cut.
Three: the diagnostic kind enum grows its own variant rather than reusing the lint kind, because reusing lint would make the response declare a kind that lies; both options bump the contract anyway, so hygiene decides.
Four: the health crate is not touched. The published purity clause for the doctor entry point is PRESERVED, and the database-derived findings are composed in the engine and folded into the report, exactly as the engine already folds in the file-state anomaly. We are minting one deliberate reversal already; a second is not paid for.
Five: the new rejection ranks after the duplicate-dependency check and before the cycle check, because a target that does not exist cannot participate in a cycle, so the specific error wins. Precedence is observable behaviour and is published, not appended silently.
Six: an external parent is legal. One shared predicate, no per-edge-type special-casing, since a carve-out applying to some edge types and not others would recreate the two-dialect split the case ruling just abolished. This is the one item worth an explicit veto if Miguel disagrees.
Seven: a listed finding carries the dependent issue id as its label and the edge type followed by the missing target as its detail, ordered deterministically so the output is snapshot-stable.
Eight: the historical run-report of the previous decision stays allow-listed as a historical record; a run-report describes a past run and is never rewritten by a later correction.

The cascade is now being applied as three disjoint patches, one per file set, each written in its own isolated worktree.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Design Review gate, round one: FAILED. Three adversarial lenses in isolated worktrees plus a coordinator, run against the landed spec cascade. Eleven blocking findings. The criterion applied was that the text must be implementable as written and must publish nothing false; it fails both, and additionally lands a required continuous-integration job red.

The orchestrator re-verified the two decisive findings by running the server rather than by reading it, and both hold.

FIRST, AND IT GOES BACK TO MIGUEL. The exporter repair he ruled silently converts blocked work into ready work. Measured on a clean workspace: an issue blocked by an ephemeral one is BLOCKED today, because the ephemeral row exists and is therefore an unresolved blocker. The exporter drops ephemeral rows; the ruled repair now also drops the edge pointing at them; so the same issue arrives READY in the destination workspace. Worse, as drafted the repair also drops PRE-EXISTING dangling edges, which would make the export command a silent laundering tool for exactly the class the new diagnostic exists to surface. This consequence was never put to him and it is his call.

SECOND, A REFRAMING THAT CHANGES ONE FIFTH OF THE SCOPE. The bulk create path was never vulnerable. Measured: a bulk document naming a non-existent blocker is already rejected today, and the rejection message reads no batch or storage match, which means that path ALREADY implements the batch-aware existence predicate the ruling asks to add everywhere else. The landed text claims that path returned success and will now return a not-found error; both halves are false. The path's only real defect is that it rejects a correctly-spelled external target. So for that entry point the work is the carve-out alone, and the path is the TEMPLATE for the predicate rather than a hole in it.

THE OTHER NINE, in brief. The published precedence chain is unbuildable as written, because the duplicate-edge rejection fires in the create wrapper AFTER the shared body where the guard is being placed, so the real order inverts the published pair; two lenses reached this independently from different directions. The required run-report gate blocks this diff, because the change touches script and rendered-roadmap paths it treats as always-substantive while the diff carries neither a run-report nor a tracker re-export. The tracker export still carries all three retired framings, and the gate row meant to catch that is vacuous, because one issue record is one physical line and its escape mode clears the whole line as soon as any comment names the new decision id. One range-pin row passes vacuously for the same family of reason, in a paragraph that congratulates itself for fixing precisely that defect. The dangling-id set is pinned to a fully-inclusive filter and then glossed as the corpus the export uses, which is a different, narrower corpus, and following the gloss would report every edge to an ephemeral row as a false finding. The round-trip obligation is hung on a property test that never touches storage, export or import, so it has no home. Two crate plans declare the widened diagnostic taxonomy in one column while pinning the old one in the test column. The wire cell that anticipates this change still passes in both worlds and its docstring is a live lie. And the new listing view executes in no continuous-integration job at all.

TWO OPEN QUESTIONS the spec writer left for this gate are resolved. The dependency-add path should also guard its edge source, in this cut, because today the same typo yields a database-level failure or a clean not-found depending on which field carries it. A foreign one-shot import file carrying a dangling edge is REJECTED rather than repaired, on the stated principle that the exporter may drop an edge but the importer may never invent one.

Next: the gate returns the work to the specification phase. This is iteration one of the two the process allows before the matter escalates.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Specification round two, and the verdicts the run-report points here for. All eleven blocking findings from the failed design gate are repaired, and an independent checker in its own worktree confirmed each one against the tree rather than against the writer's claims. Two of the eleven were only half-repairable by the writer, because their second half is a tracker action: the issue record itself carried the retired framings. That is now done — the title and the description were rewritten over the issue tool and the record re-exported, so the retired count, the retracted schema framing and the stale open question are gone from the generated export as well as from the documents.

The checker also proved the strengthened gate rows are not vacuous, by mutation: reverting the range statement on its anchored line turns the sweep red and naming the line it failed on, and restoring it turns it green again. The documentation lint was proven non-vacuous the same way, by corrupting the new decision id and watching the finding count jump. That matters here more than usual, because two of the eleven findings WERE vacuous gates that reported success while pinning nothing.

The checker then found five defects the repair itself introduced or missed, four of them real, and all five are now fixed. One sentence in the interface document still described the exporter as filtering edges, which is the last artefact of the design Miguel replaced, and it contradicted two other sentences in the same commit. A resolved-question record in the plans index still published the superseded rule that the export excludes ephemeral rows, with no pointer to the decision that amends it, and it sits inside the linted corpus where nothing would have caught the contradiction. The run-report understated its own scale, claiming nine landed non-blocking fixes where thirteen had landed. The run-report also listed absolute machine paths, in a public repository. And the readme still published the diagnostics tool as having seven actions.

Beyond those, the orchestrator landed the last three non-blocking findings rather than deferring them, so all sixteen are now closed. The two that mattered: the doc comment on the new diagnostic variant is contract bytes on both the tool side and the model side, because the schema generator lifts it into the published description that the pinned hash digests, so it is now pinned byte-for-byte and re-wording it is a contract change rather than a comment tidy-up; and the cost profile of the doctor fold is now stated instead of discovered later, since the composition differences a whole-graph edge load against a fully-inclusive issue listing on a command whose purpose is to be safe to run on a sick workspace. The single-query alternative stays deferred but now carries a measurement obligation rather than an opinion, and the previously unstated question of which side of the health feature gate the composition lives on is answered: the composition is not gated, only the fold is, so the tool action works in a build without that feature.

Every gate is green on the assembled tree: the documentation lint, the claim sweep, the knowledge lint, the formatter and the layering check. Twenty files, plus the new run-report.

Next: the design gate runs again on this text. That is round two of the two the process allows before the matter escalates to Miguel.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Design gate round two: FAILED, ten blocking findings, which under the process escalates to Miguel rather than looping. It was escalated, he ruled, and he directed a third repair pass with a closed scope followed by a final gate. No new scope, nothing already decided reopened.

THE FINDING THAT WAS HIS, and it is a hole in the ruling rather than a defect of the prose. The blocker closure as ruled follows the edges leaving an exported issue. But an issue can be blocked through an edge stored on the OTHER row: an epic is blocked by its children, and the parent-child edge lives on the child. Reproduced by running it: a durable epic blocked by an ephemeral child is blocked today, and after an export and a re-import it arrives ready, because the child row is excluded and the edge that blocked the epic left with it. So the promised property, blocked before implies blocked after, is false as written — the same silent conversion of blocked work into ready work the ruling was made to eliminate, reached through the other edge direction. HIS RULING: the closure follows incoming edges too. It pulls any excluded row that BLOCKS an exported issue, whichever side stores the edge. Equivalent and easier to read as a rule about rows: an ephemeral row that blocks something durable stops counting as ephemeral for export purposes. The set that travels is exactly the set whose absence would corrupt the destination.

TWO FURTHER FINDINGS NEEDED DECISIONS AND THE ORCHESTRATOR TOOK THEM. First, the source guard on the dependency-add path was published as ranking first while also being specified in-transaction, which is unproducible: the self-dependency rejection returns before the transaction opens. Resolved by publishing the rank the code will actually execute — the source guard sits immediately after the self-dependency check, both being questions of whether the edge is well-formed at all — and by explicitly NOT relocating the self-dependency check, which needs no transaction and whose relocation would invert a shipped pair to fix a published sentence. Second, the gate row over the generated tracker export could never go green, because the issue's own comment history legitimately quotes the retired framings, and one issue record is one physical line. Resolved the way the sibling gate already does it: the negative families are allow-listed on that path, because the file is generated wholesale and its history is a record rather than a live claim, and the teeth come instead from positive, spelling-independent landings on the same file — the record must name the decision, the five paths, and both previously-unnamed paths by their durable identifiers.

TWO OF THE TEN WERE THE ORCHESTRATOR'S OWN ERRORS, stated rather than absorbed. A sentence claiming the doctor entry point sits behind the health feature gate is false — the function exists unconditionally and only its body is conditional — and it entered through the cost note added in the previous pass. And the published action list in the readme was updated to show the new action, which violates the sequencing rule this very commit publishes: that file makes present-tense claims and is pinned exclusive on the contract version, so it moves with the code, not before it.

THE REMAINING SEVEN are one-clause edits: two live copies of the replaced exporter design surviving in the product truth and the sync crate plan, a retryability claim that contradicts the error taxonomy at three tiers, a path count that says four where the authority says three, and six stale claims that the diagnostic set still has seven kinds, two of them asserting it is unchanged.

Notable about the two rounds together: they converged, and the second round's findings are mostly residue of the design change made between them rather than new classes.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Specification round three, and the close of the specification phase. Miguel directed a closed-scope repair of the ten round-two findings followed by a final gate. The repair landed nine of the ten cleanly. The tenth — his own incoming-edge ruling — was applied everywhere the claim gate and the linters can reach, and survived in exactly three sentences, all of them in the two files that sit outside every lint corpus and outside the gate rows anchored on this task's id: one roadmap paragraph and two lines of the plans index, the latter two being the orchestrator's own wording from before the ruling existed. The independent checker and the final gate found the same three, independently, and the correct wording already existed verbatim elsewhere in the same commit. All three are now fixed, together with two non-blocking siblings, and a repository-wide sweep confirms no sentence describing either superseded exporter design survives anywhere, including the rendered roadmap.

THE MOST VALUABLE RESULT OF THIS ROUND IS A NEGATIVE ONE. The checker was asked to read the blocked-set query in full and determine whether a third blocking direction exists that nobody had named, since the second was found only after the first design had shipped. It read all three passes and established that no third direction exists: the first pass keys the blocked row's own outgoing edge, the second keys an incoming edge from a child, and the third needs only the parent's id already in the blocked set, so its propagation is carried by the outgoing direction from the kept child. An edge has two endpoints, so a walk that follows both directions and re-scans on growth yields the whole connected component over non-external edges, which is a superset of every determinant. It also checked the pool the closure draws from and found no filter that could hide a template or a closed blocker from it. The rule is complete, and that is now established by reading rather than assumed.

A LESSON THE RUN-REPORT RECORDS, because it explains all three rounds. Every survivor of this round sat where nothing lints. The claim gate's rows are anchored on this task's identifier and on the decision id, so they structurally cannot reach a paragraph that discusses the exporter without naming either. A design that changes mid-cascade needs a repository-wide sweep for the SUPERSEDED rule, not merely a check that the new rule landed somewhere. Two rounds of gates found the false claims; only an explicit negative sweep found the residue.

The final gate recommended against a fourth round and conditioned its passage on landing these edits plus that sweep. Both are done and every gate is green on the assembled tree: the documentation lint, the claim sweep, the knowledge lint, the formatter and the layering check. Nineteen files, including the run-report that covers all three passes and states plainly that the gate failed twice.

The specification is now the interface reference for the implementation, which is the next phase and the second commit: the guard itself, the shared prefix predicate, the export closure, the new diagnostics action and the doctor fold, the contract bump and its publishing sites, and the wire-level regression tests, one per guarded path, each proven to fail when its guard is removed.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Implement phase. Built in three sequential stages, each in its own isolated worktree with a private build directory, then checked by an independent verifier. What landed: the batch-aware existence guard inside the write transaction, in the shared per-record insert body and in the two sibling bodies, with the dependency-add path now guarding BOTH endpoints; one ASCII-case-insensitive external predicate at layer zero, shared by the write guard, the bulk resolver and the export walk; the export corpus widened to the transitive closure of blockers in both edge directions; a new dangling action on the diagnostics tool with the same findings folded into the command-line doctor, composed once in the engine so the health crate keeps its purity clause; the contract bump with its re-pinned hash and re-blessed goldens; and the executable claim gate this decision's zero-live-hits condition needed.

WHAT WAS PROVEN BY RUNNING, not by reading. A phantom blocker is refused on every guarded path with the published code, and the message names BOTH ids rather than only the one the caller typed. The dependency-add path's phantom SOURCE now returns a clean not-found instead of an opaque database failure, which closes the asymmetry where the same typo yielded a different exit code depending on which field carried it. A legitimate external target is accepted on every path in both letter cases, including the bulk path that rejected it before, and as a parent. And the case that forced Miguel's second ruling: a durable epic whose only open child is ephemeral, exported and imported into an EMPTY workspace, arrives still BLOCKED. The mutant that removes the incoming half of the closure is killed ONLY by the two incoming cells while the outgoing cells stay green — so that ruling is pinned by evidence rather than by prose.

THE MUTATION DISCIPLINE, INCLUDING WHERE IT DID NOT PAY OFF. Seventeen claimed kills were re-run one by one by an independent lens with checksum-verified restores; all seventeen reproduced and none was false. But three further claims were honestly downgraded rather than defended: one is an EQUIVALENT mutant that no test can distinguish, because a string carrying the external prefix can never be a row id, so neither lookup can hit it; one is redundant with a sibling skip that is genuinely killed; and one attributed to three call sites what only the shared predicate pins. Two implementers also caught false-coverage cells in their own first drafts, one of which passed in both worlds because the natural identifier ordering made a forward chain resolvable in a single pass. A later checker caught a fourth in the run-report itself. That is four false claims caught by four different mechanisms, and it is the reason the discipline is worth its cost.

THE VERIFY QUALITY GATE PASSED with five must-fixes and no loop back. Four are landed; the fifth was a knob duplicated between the specification commit and the implementation patch, now de-duplicated and both claim gates green.

TWO COSTS ARE NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED, because the specification refused to accept an opinion. The doctor fold roughly triples the doctor path on the quarter-million-issue fixture, and the number is re-derived on every run of that test rather than frozen in prose. The export closure is QUADRATIC in the excluded rows on an adversarial corpus, measured twice on two build profiles by two people: the shape is corroborated, the release absolutes are single-sourced and labelled as such because the second measurer ran out of disk. The algorithm was deliberately NOT changed here, because the worklist shape is normatively prescribed and replacing it amends the specification first. Given that export is a routine command and this project gates performance at a quarter of a million issues, that amendment is recorded as the first follow-up rather than an optional one, and it is Miguel's call.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Implement phase, landed as commit two of two. Three sequential implementers in isolated worktrees, layer by layer, each handing the next a patch, then an independent quality probe.

WHAT LANDED. The guard is bodied inside the caller's already-open transaction at all three production insert sites: the shared per-record body, which reaches the create path, both import legs and the bulk path in one edit; the dependency-add body, now guarding BOTH endpoints; and the reparent body. The predicate is batch-aware, so a forward reference inside a single import file stays legal while a phantom does not. One case-insensitive external predicate lives at the model layer and is shared by the write guard, the bulk resolver and the export walk, which is also what makes the bulk path stop rejecting a correctly-spelled external target. The exporter drops nothing and closes its corpus under blockers in both edge directions. The listing view is one composition in the engine, reached by the new diagnostics action and by the command-line doctor alike, with the health crate untouched and its purity clause intact. The contract moved to version one point eight with its hash re-pinned and every golden re-cut.

WHAT WAS PROVEN BY RUNNING, not by reading. Against a real server child process on throwaway workspaces: a phantom blocker is refused on every guarded path, with the message naming BOTH ids; the phantom SOURCE on the dependency-add path now returns the same clean not-found the target does, closing an asymmetry where the identical typo returned a database-level failure or a clean error depending only on which field carried it; an external target is accepted everywhere including the bulk path, in both letter cases, and as a parent; and a durable epic whose only open child is ephemeral is still BLOCKED after an export and a re-import into an empty workspace, which is exactly what an outgoing-only closure lost.

ON THE MUTATION DISCIPLINE, because it is the part worth keeping. Seventeen kills were reproduced by an independent lens that had not written the code. Three further claims did NOT survive that scrutiny and were downgraded in the source rather than defended: one is an equivalent mutant that no test can ever distinguish, and two were redundant sites where only the shared predicate is the real subject. Two implementers also caught false-coverage cells in their own first drafts — one of them a transitivity cell whose natural identifiers made a forward chain resolvable in a single pass, so it passed in both worlds until the chain was made order-hostile. That is the failure mode this project has shipped before, and it was caught three times in this task by three different people.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Verify quality gate: PASS with five must-fixes, all landed, no loop back to implementation. Three adversarial lenses in isolated worktrees plus a coordinator.

What the gate confirmed by execution: the guard is total over the three production write sites and runs in-transaction; a rejection leaves zero rows AND zero events; the carve-out works on all four wire paths in both letter cases; the round trip preserves blockedness in both edge directions through a real export and import into an empty workspace; the full continuous-integration probe is green; and every mutation kill it re-ran held, with zero false coverage claims surviving.

THE FIVE MUST-FIXES AND WHAT THEY WERE. One, an obligation in the interface contract required this commit to MEASURE the cost of the doctor composition on the large-workspace fixture and record the number, and no number existed. It is now measured on the existing 250 thousand issue fixture and recorded where the obligation sits, together with two honesty bounds: the fixture writes rows without dependencies, so the edge half of the cost measured zero, and the fold is a read pair, so what is recorded is caller latency rather than lock hold time. Two, a knob in the sibling gate script was duplicated verbatim, because both the specification commit and the implementation patch added it; de-duplicated. Three, an acceptance criterion demanded both letter spellings on every path and three legs carried one each; the four missing spellings were added and mutation-proved. Four, the process requires the run-report and the tracker re-export in the same commit as the work; both landed. Five, the specification stated that the export closure terminates but never what it costs.

THAT LAST ONE IS THE FINDING WORTH READING TWICE. The closure is quadratic in the excluded rows in its worst case, and the worst case is constructible entirely through the public interface: one kept row plus a chain of ephemeral rows whose identifiers ascend along the chain, so the natural listing order is the exact reverse of eligibility order and each pass pulls in only the last row it scans. Measured through the real export path on a release build at four, eight, sixteen and thirty-two thousand excluded rows: 327 milliseconds, 1.21 seconds, 5.06 seconds and 24.6 seconds, against a linear control of 59, 75, 123 and 238 milliseconds. A second measurer reproduced the SHAPE on a debug build and could not build release, so the release absolutes are recorded as single-sourced and the specification says so and says to re-derive them before quoting them as a budget. The faster shape — a both-direction stack seeded from the kept set over the two maps the code already builds — is DELIBERATELY not in this commit: the worklist shape is prescribed by the very clause that discloses the cost, so replacing it amends that clause first and is Miguel's call under the no-simplify rule. Export is a command this repository runs on every commit, so this is a real risk and not a theoretical one; it is the first follow-up below.

Follow-up work the two gates identified, recorded here rather than absorbed silently. None of it blocks this change; each is named so it can be picked up or dismissed on its merits.

One and most important: linearize the export closure to a both-direction stack seeded from the kept set, removing the quadratic term. It needs the interface clause amended first, because that clause prescribes the current shape, so it is Miguel's decision and not an implementation detail. Two: a crate-wide sweep in the storage crate for the message-clipping helper, which has zero call sites there while eleven pre-existing not-found constructions pass an identifier through unclipped; the new code follows the crate convention rather than diverging from it, and the class is already disclosed in the product truth, but the convention itself is the defect. Three: the same asymmetry this task closed on the dependency-add path still survives on the create path, where a mistyped parent reaches a foreign-key failure and returns exit two rather than the clean exit three the sibling now returns. Four: forward the storage context through the sync boundary so the import refusal is machine-readable rather than only human-readable. Five: detaching a parent by passing an explicit null is unreachable on the wire. Six: scope the checked-target set per batch rather than per call. Seven: publish the rejection precedence as per-record and pin the cross-record case. Eight: decide and state whether an external target's suffix gets a shape bound at all.

Track phase. Branch pushed and pull request 435 opened against main: https://github.com/websublime/unblock/pull/435

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Continuous integration on the pull request: eighteen checks pass, four skip because they are release-pipeline jobs that do not run on a pull request, and ONE fails — the 250 thousand issue scale gate. Notably the hybrid performance gate, historically the flakiest job here, passed, so the failure is a real cost and not noise.

THE FAILURE, measured rather than guessed. On the continuous-integration runner at 250 thousand issues the pre-existing integrity check costs 5.51 seconds, the new dangling fold costs 10.72 seconds, and the doctor command totals 16.31 seconds against a 15 second boundedness guard. The cause was structural: the composition read the whole dependency graph and then every issue row through fully-inclusive filters and diffed them in memory. The standalone diagnostics action paid the same cost with no test watching it, so the doctor fold was merely where a test happened to catch it.

MIGUEL RULED: move the composition into one SQL query. He was offered raising the guard and dropping the fold from the doctor, and rejected both — the guard had just done its job, and dropping the fold would have left the diagnostics action equally slow and unwatched.

WHAT LANDED, specification first because the interface contract pinned the opposite: that no new trait method was needed, since the graph loader does no join. That reasoning was true and its cost had simply never been measured. The superseded text and its numbers are kept quoted in place rather than overwritten, because they are the evidence that forced the change. A new trait method returns only the edges whose target row is absent, via a left join excluding external targets with the same case-insensitive semantics as the shared predicate, in the pinned order; all twelve implementors were updated, and the two fakes in the sync crate were given honest bodies rather than an empty stub that would have made that crate vacuously green.

THE TRAP SURVIVED THE REWRITE, which was the thing most likely to go wrong. The old clause demanded a fully-inclusive id set precisely because the default filters exclude closed and tombstoned rows and would report every closed blocker as dangling. In the query that becomes a join on EXISTENCE ALONE and never on status. It is pinned at both layers and mutation-proved: making the join condition status-aware turns both cells red, naming the closed and the tombstoned blocker.

MEASURED AFTER, by two people independently at 250 thousand: the fold went from 4.51 seconds to 88.7 microseconds, about fifty-one thousand times faster, and the doctor command from 7.00 to 2.53 seconds, which is essentially just the integrity check that was always there. The guard was not touched.

ONE HONESTY BOUND, disclosed rather than buried: the scale corpus has an EMPTY dependency table, so it does not exercise the new query at all. Measured separately on 250 thousand issues WITH 250 thousand edges: 111 milliseconds when every edge resolves, 403 milliseconds when none do. The cost holds, but no test yet enforces that bound, and that is the next follow-up.

description:
Split out of ub-lp9.20 by Miguel's ruling during that issue's Decide phase, and ruled to ship in the SAME 1.0.1 cut as a co-requisite of it. THIS DESCRIPTION WAS REWRITTEN ON 2026-08-01 after the Understand and Decide phases and the first design-review gate; three framings it previously carried are RETIRED and are recorded here only so nobody re-derives them.

WHAT WAS RETIRED. It is NOT a missing foreign key: dependencies.depends_on_id deliberately carries none, because an external target is a legitimate blocker no foreign key could satisfy, so the repair is application-level and no schema change is authorised. It is NOT three edge-writing paths: there are five. And it does NOT mint no decision id: it mints D45, because Miguel's ruling puts the guard in the shared per-record insert body, which reverses a clause D44 published.

THE DEFECT, reproduced live over the MCP wire on a clean workspace. An edge may name a blocker that does not exist. The call returns success with no error, and the affected issue acquires a blocker that can never be created and therefore never closed - so for the three gating edge types it can never re-enter the ready set through any normal operation.

THE FIVE EDGE-WRITING PATHS, and which are actually vulnerable. Four accept a non-existent blocker with isError false: issue create with seeded deps, dep add, the JSONL import, and the one-shot bd import. The fifth, issue create_bulk, was NEVER vulnerable - measured, it already rejects an unknown blocker and its message reads no batch or storage match, so it ALREADY implements the batch-aware existence predicate this task adds everywhere else. That path is therefore the TEMPLATE for the predicate, not a hole in it; its only real defect is that it rejects a correctly-spelled external target, which the carve-out relaxes. A sixth observation: the reparent path plants a phantom parent, which is a real dangling edge and a subject for the listing view, but it does NOT make the child unready - parent-child is not a gating type.

WHY IT SHIPS WITH ub-lp9.20. D44 strictly increases exposure: the foreign-key failure on the edge SOURCE that used to mask a bogus blocker id no longer occurs, because the source id has left the wire.

MIGUEL'S RULINGS (2026-07-31 and 2026-08-01), all recorded in the comment thread. Guard every path, with the check in the shared per-record body and a batch-aware predicate. The external prefix is case-insensitive, on the principle that the write guard is never stricter than the read side. Close all five paths. The listing view is a new action on the diagnostics tool plus the same findings folded into the doctor report. And the exporter, rather than dropping an orphaned edge, EXPORTS THE TRANSITIVE CLOSURE OF BLOCKERS, so an ephemeral blocker travels with its dependent and nothing silently turns blocked work into ready work; that supersedes the published clause excluding ephemeral rows from export, riding D45 rather than a new id.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- The behaviour is reproduced live from every edge-writing path and documented. DONE, in the comment thread.
- The import question is put to Miguel and his ruling recorded before implementation. DONE.
- No input on a guarded path can persist an edge whose blocker neither exists nor carries the external prefix.
- The external carve-out is preserved and tested on every path, including the bulk path that rejects it today.
- The new diagnostics action and the doctor report both list the dangling blockers already present in a live workspace, and the listing executes in a continuous-integration job.
- Export then import into an empty workspace SUCCEEDS on any corpus the tool itself produced, and an issue blocked before the export is blocked after it.
- An export of a workspace that ALREADY holds dangling edges produces a file the import refuses, naming the first offending pair; the remedy is the new diagnostic. This is disclosed, not silent.
- Regression tests at the live wire level, one per guarded path, each naming the mutant it kills and proven to fail when the guard is removed.
- Ships in the 1.0.1 cut, with the contract bump and the decision-range bump.
